description: We are interested in science, research, and creative problem-solving. We enjoy researching topics, exploring possible solutions, brainstorming ideas, and presenting them clearly. We are looking forward to collaborating with a team, learning from each other, and turning a creative idea into a meaningful project for NASA Space Apps.
summary: CAPCOM: Storm Watch is a web game for kids aged 7-12. The player is CAPCOM, the voice of mission control, and guides a Moon crew and a Mars crew through four real space-weather events from NASA records, with help from a robot guide called SOL. Each choice costs power, safety or time, so kids learn how astronauts survive radiation storms, power shortages and radio delay. It answers the "Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge by turning real NASA data into a short, fun, voiced training mission that works in any browser.
details:
What it does: the player acts as CAPCOM and talks to the crew by radio. Levels use real NASA events: the Sept 2017 X8.2 solar flare, the May 2024 G5 geomagnetic storm, the July 2012 near miss (read NASA's real forecast map), and the June 2018 global dust storm on Mars. Players choose a base site on the real Moon, build shielding, manage power for air and heat, keep food growing, and write rules in advance because of a 12-minute radio delay. Every choice has a visible cost. Levels unlock in order and can be replayed.

How it works: a static website with a Vercel serverless function (api/donki.js) that reads NASA DONKI on the server, so the NASA API key never reaches the browser. A "Today's real Sun" panel shows the last 30 days of real space weather.

Goals and benefits: teach space-weather safety, resource management and decision-making to kids 7-12. Every line is voiced and shown as subtitles, the text is simple, and a short "How to play" screen starts the game. Storms and dates are real; the crews and meter numbers are imagined "game points", and the game says so on screen.

We hope that any child who completes the game will be able to explain, in their own words, four real constraints of living off Earth. It reaches children aged 7–12 at home or in class, teachers (who receive an offline copy and an "About the data" page), and parents or older siblings.

Tools: JavaScript, HTML, CSS, three.js (3D Moon, Mars and base), a 3D robot model (SOL), Node serverless function on Vercel, Python for the build script and voice generation (Kokoro TTS). Security headers (CSP, HSTS) are set in vercel.json. No accounts, no tracking; progress is saved only in the player's browser. No special hardware: it runs on a phone, tablet or computer with a modern browser.
